result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Comparison.to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Get the comparison results as a JSON string. twitter-card: title: >- [Comparison.to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Get the comparison results as a JSON string. title: >- [Comparison.to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get the comparison results as a JSON string. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the comparison results as a JSON string. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/_compare.py#L2379-L2437){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Comparison.to_json( samples=True, limit=10, indent=2, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} JSON is the format to use when a comparison result leaves Python: written to a file alongside a pipeline run, returned from an API, or read by another tool. The structure is the same as that of [`to_dict()`](`pointblank.Comparison.to_dict`). The `pb compare` command line tool produces the same JSON with `--format json` (to the terminal) or `--output-json` (to a file), and its `--no-samples` option corresponds to `samples=False`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [samples]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should samples of differing rows be included? Set to `False` when the data might contain sensitive values (e.g., PII) and only counts and schema details may be stored. [limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The maximum number of sample rows per status. [indent]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The number of spaces to indent nested levels by. Use `None` for the most compact output, on a single line (as for JSON Lines files, with one comparison per line). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The comparison results as a JSON string. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Here, a new version of a price list has one changed price. ::: {#814f4570 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl prices_v1 = pl.DataFrame({"sku": ["A-1", "A-2", "A-3"], "price": [9.99, 24.50, 5.00]}) prices_v2 = pl.DataFrame({"sku": ["A-1", "A-2", "A-3"], "price": [9.99, 26.00, 5.00]}) comparison = pb.compare(prices_v1, prices_v2, keys="sku") print(comparison.to_json(limit=5)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` { "source_name": "source", "target_name": "target", "mode": "keyed", "keys": [ "sku" ], "compared_columns": [ "price" ], "column_map": {}, "schema_mode": "strict", "null_equal": true, "partitions": 1, "n_source_rows": 3, "n_target_rows": 3, "n": 3, "n_passed": 2, "n_failed": 1, "identical": false, "status_counts": { "match": 2, "changed": 1, "missing": 0, "extra": 0, "dup_key": 0 }, "column_mismatches": { "price": 1 }, "schema_diff": { "matches": true, "only_in_source": [], "only_in_target": [], "dtype_changed": [], "renamed": [], "case_only": [], "reordered": false }, "samples": { "changed": [ { "sku": "A-2", "price_source": 24.5, "price_target": 26.0 } ] } } ``` ::: ::: For a compact record without row samples, set `samples=False` and `indent=None`: ::: {#7c922089 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(comparison.to_json(samples=False, indent=None)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` {"source_name": "source", "target_name": "target", "mode": "keyed", "keys": ["sku"], "compared_columns": ["price"], "column_map": {}, "schema_mode": "strict", "null_equal": true, "partitions": 1, "n_source_rows": 3, "n_target_rows": 3, "n": 3, "n_passed": 2, "n_failed": 1, "identical": false, "status_counts": {"match": 2, "changed": 1, "missing": 0, "extra": 0, "dup_key": 0}, "column_mismatches": {"price": 1}, "schema_diff": {"matches": true, "only_in_source": [], "only_in_target": [], "dtype_changed": [], "renamed": [], "case_only": [], "reordered": false}} ``` ::: ::: Each such record is one line, so a series of comparisons can be appended to a single file and read back later, one comparison per line.
